name: Zenato Amarone della Valpolicella Classico Sergio Zenato Riserva 2010
text:
## Zenato Amarone della Valpolicella Classico Sergio Zenato Riserva 2010

**The story.** Zenato is based at [Peschiera del Garda](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Zenato,+Via+San+Benedetto+8,+Peschiera+del+Garda,+Italy&t=k) on the southern shore of [Lake Garda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Garda), and makes wine in the [Valpolicella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valpolicella) hills in the province of [Verona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verona). Its founder, Sergio Zenato, created the 35-hectare Costalunga estate in Valpolicella Classica, shaped with dry stone walls that preserve "the vine's essential balance: air, water and warmth" ([Zenato](https://www.zenato.it/en/the-estates/costalunga-estate/)). This Riserva, the estate's top Amarone, "proudly bears the signature of our founder" ([Zenato, technical sheet](https://www.zenato.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/AMARONE-RISERVA_EN.pdf)).

**What Amarone is.** [Amarone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarone) is made from grapes that are dried before fermentation, a process called *appassimento*: the bunches are laid out, traditionally on bamboo racks, to shrivel, concentrating their sugar and flavour. The wine is then fermented dry. "Amarone" means "great bitter", to distinguish it from the region's sweet [Recioto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valpolicella). Although Valpolicella has made notable wines since ancient times, the name Amarone was probably coined only in 1936, and the wine wasn't marketed under it before 1953 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarone)).

**The wine: Riserva Sergio Zenato.** Zenato's sheet gives the blend as 85% [Corvina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corvina), 10% [Rondinella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rondinella), and 5% [Oseleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oseleta) and Croatina, from the estate's oldest vines, averaging 30 years, at Sant'Ambrogio di Valpolicella, at 300 to 350 metres on stony chalk-limestone. The grapes are hand-picked into small 5-kg crates and dried for about four months in airy drying rooms; only in January are they crushed. After 15 to 20 days of fermentation on the skins, the wine ages about five years in large Slavonian oak casks and at least a year in bottle ([Zenato, technical sheet](https://www.zenato.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/AMARONE-RISERVA_EN.pdf)). The estate describes maraschino cherry, dried plum and fig, tobacco, leather, sweet spice, licorice and balsamic notes, and serves it at 18°C.

**The vintage.** Jancis Robinson's vintage charts don't cover the Veneto. With five years in cask and a year in bottle, this 2010 was released only around 2016.

**What the critics say for 2010.**
- **Andreas Larsson: 91** (February 2017, [his tasting notes](https://www.andreas-larsson.com/tasting/zenato-riserva-sergio-zenato-2010)). A complex, slightly mature nose of ripe dark fruit, sweet cherry, plum and cigar box; rich, ripe and unctuous, with a touch of alcohol but balanced acidity and fine tannin, tobacco-scented dark fruit, spice and leather, and a long, warm finish. "Bold and rich but with good balance."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.3** (from your CellarTracker list), the highest score in this batch.
- (Retail pages list James Suckling and Wine Spectator scores, but I couldn't read the notes themselves, so I've left them out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2034. Amarone of this structure ages beautifully: expect dried cherry, fig, tobacco, leather and spice. Open it any time over the next several years; decant one to two hours ahead and serve at about 18°C, as the estate suggests.

**Food.** Zenato suggests roast game, grilled red meat and aged cheeses, or simply sipping it as a "contemplative wine" ([Zenato](https://www.zenato.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/AMARONE-RISERVA_EN.pdf)). My picks: [risotto all'Amarone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risotto), braised beef cheeks, roast venison, or a chunk of aged [Monte Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Veronese) or [Parmigiano Reggiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parmesan).

**Value and where to buy.** The Amarone isn't listed in the stores on this site, but BSW Liquor carries Zenato's white Lugana Riserva Sergio Zenato 2022 at $47.99.

**From the history books**
- **A late name for an old wine.** The Amarone name is believed to have been coined by Adelino Lucchese in 1936 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarone)).
- **DOCG in 2009.** Amarone became a DOC in December 1990 and was promoted to DOCG, Italy's top category, on 4 December 2009 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarone)).

**Curious details**
- **Bitter versus sweet.** Amarone's name, "great bitter", was coined to set it apart from the sweet Recioto made from the same dried grapes ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amarone)).
